intro: Chapter 7 returns to narrative. At the Lord's command, Lehi's sons journey back to Jerusalem a second time — now to bring **Ishmael and his family** into the wilderness, so that Lehi's sons may marry and raise up seed in the promised land. Ishmael's household agrees and sets out with them, but on the way **Laman, Lemuel, and part of Ishmael's family rebel** and want to return to Jerusalem. **Nephi rebukes them**, recalling the angel they saw, the deliverance from Laban, and the coming destruction of Jerusalem, and calling them to faith. Enraged, they bind him with cords to leave him to perish, but Nephi prays and the **bands are loosed by the power of faith**. When some of Ishmael's family plead for him, his brothers repent, ask forgiveness, and are freely pardoned; the company reaches Lehi's tent and offers **sacrifice and burnt offerings** to the Lord.

entries.title: Grammar: Compound verbs with کردن and شدن
entries.body: Persian builds most of its verbs by pairing a noun or adjective with a **light verb** that carries the tense, person, and mood. `کردن` "do" makes active senses and `شدن` "become" makes inchoative or passive ones; the first word supplies the meaning, the light verb the grammar. This chapter's summary is a chain of them.

entries.title: Grammar: The subjunctive of purpose after تا
entries.body: `تا` "so that, in order to" opens a clause of **purpose**, and its verb stands in the **subjunctive** — the mood of intended or unrealized action. A simple verb takes the prefix `بـ-` (`برویم`, `بگیرند`); a compound verb usually drops it and leaves the bare present stem (`همراه شوند`). The subjunctive never takes `می-`.

entries.title: Grammar: چنین گذشت — "and it came to pass"
entries.body: The narrative formula `و چنین گذشت که …` — literally "and thus it passed that …" — is the Persian Book of Mormon's calque of the King James "and it came to pass that …." `چنین` "thus" + `گذشت` (3sg past of `گذشتن` "to pass") opens nearly every episode of the chapter. It is a discourse marker, not a statement about time, and is best read simply as "then."

entries.title: Grammar: The object marker را
entries.body: The particle `را` _rā_ marks a **definite direct object**, and it follows the *whole* object phrase — after any possessive, ezafe chain, or modifier — not just the bare noun. Because Persian puts the verb last, `را` is the reader's signal that everything before it is the thing being acted upon.

examples.persian: خانواده اش را تنها به بیابان ببرد
examples.translit: xānevāde-aš rā tanhā be bīyābān be-barad
examples.en: that he take his family into the wilderness alone

entries.title: Grammar: Possessive and pronominal suffixes
entries.body: Persian attaches possession directly to the noun as an enclitic: `-am` (my), `-at` (your sg.), `-aš` (his/her), `-mān` (our), `-tān` (your pl.), `-šān` (their). After a plural in `-ān` the linking vowel appears (`برادرانم` _barādarān-am_). The same clitic on a verb or preposition serves as an object pronoun (`مرا` = `من` + `را`).

entries.title: Grammar: Archaic biblical register
entries.body: To match the scriptural voice, the Persian text reaches for archaic and literary forms. The narrative `-ا` on `گفتا` _goftā_ "and he said" is a storytelling past; the vocative `-ا` on `سَروَرا` _Sarvarā_ "O Lord" is the form of direct address; `بنگرید` _benegarīd_ "behold" and `آری` _ārī_ "yea" are bookish attention-words; and `سَروَر` "the Lord" (lit. "master, chief") renders the divine name throughout.

entries.title: Grammar: The perfect tense (past participle + copula)
entries.body: The perfect — "have done" — is the **past participle** (in `-ه`, e.g. `کرده`, `دیده`) plus the enclitic present copula (`-ام`, `-ای`, `-است`, `-ایم`, `-اید`, `-اند`). The participle stays fixed; the copula agrees with the subject. Nephi hammers his brethren with it: what have ye *forgotten*, what have ye *not accepted*.

entries.title: Grammar: The future tense (خواهد + short infinitive)
entries.body: Formal Persian marks the definite future with the auxiliary `خواستن` "to want" — conjugated for person (`خواهم`, `خواهی`, `خواهد` …) — followed by the **short infinitive** (the bare past stem: `آورد`, `دانست`, `شد`). The auxiliary comes first and takes no `می-`. This formal future belongs to the scriptural register of Nephi's prophecy.

entries.title: Grammar: The passive voice with شدن
entries.body: Persian has no inflected passive; it uses the **past participle** of the main verb plus a form of `شدن` "to become": `برآورده شد` "was fulfilled" (lit. "became fulfilled"). The participle is invariable and `شدن` carries tense, person, and mood — including the subjunctive `شوم` "(that) I be."

[`نا-`](../word_formation.html#n-un-non-in) + [`بکار`](../word_formation.html#be-in-with-by) ([به‌-](../word_formation.html#be-in-with-by) + `کار` "work") + `-ی` ([abstract suffix](../word_formation.html#the-abstract-noun-suffix-g)) → "non-useful-ness, wickedness".

entries.family: [`نا-`](../word_formation.html#n-un-non-in) _nā-_ (privative prefix); `کار` _kār_ "work" (an entry in this chapter); `نابکار` _nābekār_ "wicked, useless" (the underlying adjective).

etym.prose: `اندوه` _anduh_ (grief, sorrow) + [`-گین`](../word_formation.html#the-suffix-gin) (laden-with suffix).
native Persian; from older _fra-rūd-_ "down-flow".

entries.meaning: to forgive, pardon; to bestow, give

etym.prose: `آن` + `چه` → fused relative pronoun.
[`به‌-`](../word_formation.html#be-in-with-by) + `راستی` (← `راست` + `-ی`).

entries.meaning: threshold, gateway; the (royal or divine) presence, court

etym.prose: `در` "door" + [`گاه`](../word_formation.html#g-h-place-or-time-of-x) "place, time" → "door-place, threshold."
native Persian; from Old Persian _xvadāta-_ "lord, self-existing".
from Arabic, root s-f-r "to travel"; verbal-noun pattern _mufāʿalat_.

entries.meaning: to arrive, to reach (3pl pres. _می رسند mī-rasand_)

forms.note: Suppletive present stem `آ`/`آی` _ā-/āy-_ (e.g. `می‌آید` _mī-āyad_), unrelated to the past stem `آمد`.

etym.prose: `سپاس` "thanks, gratitude" + `گزار` (← `گذاشتن` "to place") + `-ی` ([abstract suffix](../word_formation.html#the-abstract-noun-suffix-g)) → "the placing/laying down of thanks."
